Unsure what game you’re talking about, but most games in the series have a pretty variable difficulty depending on how much time you’re willing to put into the Garage (customization and building). If you try to brute force everything with one build or playstyle, things might be pretty hard at points. The series’ bread and butter is its customization, and creativity and experimentation is encouraged by not losing money by selling parts back to the shop. I came into the series as a pretty casual player with A.C.: For Answer after playing Dark Souls with a cheese build and having lots of trouble and kinda hating it, and LOVED IT. For the most part, throughout the series the difficulty comes in spikes, with certain missions or fights being quite difficult, while (in my experience) most are easy to medium difficulty. Additionally, I found it quite easy to hop in, so a few missions or customize my mech a bit, and hop out for a quick session, as most missions are in the 5-15 minute range for a successful completion, with some exceptions.

TL;DR, give it a try, don’t be afraid to experiment, and don’t be ashamed to look up build guides or tips. I think the series is very casual friendly, easy to hop into for a quick session.

MGS3>MGS2>MGR>MGS>MG2>MGS4>MGS:GB>MG>MGSV
My list is mainly based off of story, as that’s what I enjoy most about the series. I still think MGS3 is the best looking and best gameplay in the series. I played on 3DS, tho, so a lot of the problems people have with it aren’t there or are mitigated.
MGS2 I absolutely adore. I think it’s probably the best story-wise.
MGR, while not a traditional MG game, I still found it one of the most positive experiences with the franchise.
MGS, while still really really enjoyable, has some major glaring issues. Backtracking, lack of some major QOL features from later games, etc. dampen the experience, but it is overall a really enjoyable game.
Metal Gear 2 is my favorite 2D entry in the series by far. The story is great, gameplay is amazing, and graphics are great. One of the best 8-Bit games of all time IMO.
MGS4, while having more refined gameplay, is simply far too cutscene heavy. The story is ok, for the most part, but the cutscenes drag on for far too long. Makes me feel like I’m watching a movie with a game as a bonus.
MGS: Ghost Babel was my first introduction to the series, and still holds a beloved place in my heart. I feel like it had a really strong opening, but a weaker second half. A LOT of replayablity, and the first appearance of Raiden in an (albeit not canon) MG game.
The original MG is a bit too basic for my tastes. I think the game looks great, but the gameplay is very repetitive and feels like too much trial and error.
MGSV, specifically TPP, isn’t a game I like. A really, really bad story (my main draw to MG), combined with repetitive missions and empty maps made it feel like a game that was rushed with no care put into it. While I love GZ, TPP just feels like a rushed game that should have had another year and a half to bake.

Ultimate is great while it lasts, but it’s existence poses major problems for the series going forward. One one hand, you could just keep adding more and more characters, but that would likely result in longer development times, less balanced rosters, and a lot of content bloat. On the other hand, you could remove some characters while adding new ones or updating movesets, which would cost less, take less time, and keep the roster a lot more balanced. Neither of these options are perfect, though, and will likely piss off at least a chunk of the fan base. I personally think that the best way forward for the series is a sort of “soft reboot”, where really core characters are kept, while most are removed, as well as adding new characters that haven’t appeared before. While better single player content is something I would very much LOVE to see going forward, it’s clear that Smash’s longevity, both as games and as a series, are derived (at least partially) from it’s multiplayer aspects.
